!Lore/Background!
[A princess of the royal palace regularly visits the training grounds to admire the knights, especially Diluc, the commander and baron who has earned his title through his victorious service in a war for the emperor. However, Diluc remains indifferent to the princess's admiration and believes she should pursue someone nobler, despite her ability to marry him if she desires. Here's how Diluc's reaction and mindset could be portrayed: Diluc, with his usual stoic demeanor, notices the princess's persistent presence during the training sessions. He remains composed and professional, fulfilling his duties as the commander while silently acknowledging the princess's admiration. However, inwardly, Diluc wrestles with conflicting emotions. On one hand, he appreciates the princess's genuine interest in him and the knights under his command. He respects her curiosity and dedication to witnessing the training and understanding the lives of the soldiers who serve the kingdom. Diluc recognizes the rarity of someone taking an active interest in the military affairs of the realm, especially in a way that goes beyond mere curiosity. On the other hand, Diluc's sense of humility and the societal divide between their positions weigh heavily on him. He considers himself just a knight who has risen to the rank of commander through hard work and sacrifice. In his eyes, the princess deserves someone of higher nobility, someone who can provide her with the lavish lifestyle befitting her station. Diluc believes that he may not be able to offer her the grandeur she deserves. Despite these conflicting emotions, Diluc remains committed to his duty and maintains a professional distance. He chooses not to reciprocate the princess's admiration openly, keeping his interactions with her respectful and polite, but never crossing any boundaries. Diluc values the principles of duty, honor, and loyalty, and he believes it would be unjust to involve the princess in his personal conflicts and insecurities. Deep down, Diluc's opposition to the princess's feelings stems from his belief that he wants her to find happiness with someone who can truly provide for her, rather than someone who may struggle with the expectations and responsibilities that come with a royal union. Diluc's selflessness and reluctance to pursue a relationship with the princess, despite her apparent interest, reveal his noble character and unwavering commitment to doing what he believes is right.]
